page: Amazon Web Services c6id.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processor (Ice Lake 8375C) clocked at 3.5 GHz. The instance allocates 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 128 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Network performance features a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the server does not include GPU acceleration.

A defining hardware characteristic of the c6id family is the inclusion of integrated high-speed storage. The c6id.16xlarge provides 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. This ephemeral storage configuration delivers low-latency disk access directly to host workloads without consuming external block storage network allocations. Compute instruction extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA extensions, enhancing vector calculations, cryptography, and parallel processing.

Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier capabilities across parallel execution and data operations. The instance scores in the top quartile for PassMark CPU overall, extended instructions, encryption, and database operations. Real-world tasks such as software compilation using Clang, ray tracing, image processing, static web serving throughput (45.17 GB/s), and small-to-medium model LLM text generation also land in the top 25 percent. Conversely, baseline stress-ng multi-core metrics, standard Geekbench general multi-core scores, and memory bandwidth benchmarks perform within the middle 50 percent.

Balancing a high compute-to-memory density with massive local NVMe capacity, the c6id.16xlarge yields strong qualitative cost efficiency for applications that demand high-speed temporary disk caching alongside parallel CPU execution. The architecture is best aligned with large-scale distributed compilation pipelines, static web serving, high-performance computing (HPC), relational database testing, and media encoding tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.16xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores), 128 GB of DDR4 memory, and 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating with a 25 Gbps baseline network capacity and no dedicated GPUs, the instance maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio tailored for compute-heavy applications. Benchmark testing reveals top-quartile execution in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, image processing, PassMark database operations, and high-throughput static web serving. Vector acceleration is supported via AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. With its fast local storage and dense compute footprint, the c6id.16xlarge is well aligned for distributed continuous integration builds, relational database workloads requiring low-latency local scratch space, media rendering, and batch compute processing.
